page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-standard-2 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor using the x86_64 architecture. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with 2 threads per core. The instance is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include bundled local storage or GPU accelerators, and comes with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The underlying CPU includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, alongside hardware support for AVX, AES, VAES, and SHA_NI cryptographic instructions.

Benchmark data reveals a distinct performance profile. The instance demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance in stress-ng tests, placing in the top 25%. However, its multi-core scaling is limited, with stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core scores falling into the bottom 25% and bottom 10% respectively. Memory performance is a notable bottleneck; read-only small block memory bandwidth is poor, while large block read and write bandwidths are weak. This resource constraint is reflected in database operations, Redis SET performance, and static web serving throughput, all of which rank in the bottom 10%.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the n2d-standard-2 offers a low-cost entry point for workloads that require dedicated CPU allocation but do not demand high memory bandwidth or intensive multi-threaded processing. It is best suited for lightweight, single-threaded applications, basic text processing, simple scripting, and low-traffic web serving. It is less suitable for memory-bound databases, parallel software compilation, or real-time image and physics processing due to its constrained memory throughput and multi-core limitations.
